findings.title: Signing into another account retains the previous account's persistence state
findings.problem: noteAccountRead permanently refuses a different user once state.user is set. App.jsx keeps accountRead, acceptedBlob, loadedBaseline, and progressGate at module scope, but signing out does not clear them. A legitimate account switch therefore returns the new account's read without rebinding the adapter, and subsequent saves merge against the previous account's blob.
findings.failure_scenario: Account A studies, signs out, and account B signs in without reloading the page. B's first autosave can union A's answer history into B's progress and persist it there, exposing A's study history and corrupting B's stats.
findings.fix: Scope persistence state to the signed-in account or App instance. Invalidate reads and writes on authentication transitions, and reject late responses using an account/request epoch rather than rejecting every different user. Add an integration test that signs A out and B in within the same page and verifies that neither account's blob contains the other's history.

findings.title: Successive saves repeatedly add already-saved XP and best-run gains
findings.problem: reconcileProgress adds both snapshots' cumulative deltas from baselineBlob. App.jsx leaves loadedBaseline fixed at the initial read while acceptedBlob advances after each save. Consequently, a later save adds progress that was already accepted. Returning the inflated blob as reconciled then triggers another autosave, which can repeat the inflation indefinitely. bestRun is also incorrectly treated as an additive counter.
findings.failure_scenario: Load an existing row with 0 XP, earn and save 10 XP, then change the theme. The next reconciliation calculates 0 + 10 + 10 = 20 XP. Applying that result triggers another save calculating 40 XP, then 80 XP, despite no further answers.
findings.fix: Track the last acknowledged local snapshot and merge only unacknowledged changes, advancing the reconciliation baseline appropriately after successful writes. Merge bestRun by maximum, not addition. Add a real-adapter test covering an answer save followed by several non-answer saves and assert that XP and bestRun remain unchanged.

findings.title: Legacy history rows with the same hash are overwritten by the last row
findings.problem: progressRowKey is not unique for legacy answers: it excludes category, source, and canonical key, and legacy rows commonly lack attempt, day, at, and ms. mergeLogs stores only the last local row for each such hash, then substitutes that row for every matching server row. This corrupts history even during an ordinary first autosave.
findings.failure_scenario: A migrated history contains bank:7 and builtin:7, both answered incorrectly before timestamps and attempt IDs existed. Both hash to h:7:false:::. The autosave replaces both records with whichever appears last, undoing the migration's source distinction. Repeated legacy misses can likewise all be relabeled when the student identifies only one.
findings.fix: Give legacy occurrences stable unique identities, or reconcile legacy edits against their specific baseline occurrence without collapsing multiplicity. Do not use this lossy hash as a row identifier. Test two distinct canonical questions sharing a numeric ID and two repeated legacy answers where only one occurrence is edited.

findings.title: Conflict recovery merges answers but discards one device's scored state
findings.problem: When both devices changed ability, reconciliation keeps only local.ability despite unioning both answer logs. The same whole-object selection loses concurrent changes to missSchedule, srsMap, rewards, and daily. The resulting persisted log and ability evidence disagree, so readiness and adaptivity no longer represent the recorded answers.
findings.failure_scenario: Two devices load the same baseline and each answer a different question. After the revision conflict, both answers appear in the merged log, but ability contains only one device's updates. If both answers were misses, one review schedule can disappear; concurrent grades of different flashcards can also lose one schedule.
findings.fix: Reconcile complete progress changes, not just log rows. Apply each previously unseen answer's deterministic scoring effects in a defined order against the shared baseline, preserving legacy starting ability, and merge independent schedule and ledger entries without replacing entire maps. Test concurrent nonzero-XP answers in different categories and concurrent grades of different cards.

findings.title: Stale reconciliation results are applied before the stale-result guard
findings.problem: The autosave callback calls applyBlob(res.blob) before checking res.stale. createSaveQueue explicitly returns reconciled payloads even when their save has become stale, so an obsolete snapshot can replace newer in-memory answers, XP, ability, and schedules.
findings.failure_scenario: A conflict-recovery save is awaiting its response when the student answers another question. The older save completes with a reconciled blob that lacks the new answer and is marked stale. App.jsx nevertheless installs it, rolling back the visible progress and generating another autosave from the obsolete state, which can supersede the queued newer snapshot.
findings.fix: Reject stale, aborted, or wrong-account results before applying any blob. Also ensure reconciliation cannot replace state that advanced beyond the snapshot being acknowledged. Add a browser test that holds a reconciled save response, records another answer, releases the response, and verifies that the newer answer survives both in memory and after reload.

assessment: Do not ship. The persistence changes contain account-isolation, XP, history-corruption, and readiness defects. The warfarin correction and supplied image changes look sound. I could not execute the tests from the supplied review material.
